data.title: Muscle Tissue
data.definition: Muscle is a specialised tissue of mesodermal origin that contracts to produce movement.
data.caption: Types of muscle fibres

items.title: Excitability
items.text: Responds to a nerve impulse or other stimulus

items.title: Extensibility
items.text: Can be stretched beyond its resting length

items.title: Elasticity
items.text: Returns to its original shape after stretching

items.title: Conductivity
items.text: Carries the impulse along the whole fibre

items.title: Fatigue
items.text: Repeated activity builds up lactic acid

data.title: Sliding Filament Theory
data.caption: Cross-bridge formation between actin and myosin

sections.heading: Mechanism / Concept used
sections.text: Muscle contracts when thin actin filaments slide over thick myosin filaments; the filaments themselves do not shorten.

sections.heading: Key steps
points: Ca²⁺ binds troponin and exposes actin sites
Power stroke pulls actin towards the M-line

data.title: Solved Example
data.problem: A sarcomere is 2.4 µm long at rest. During contraction each I-band shortens by 0.2 µm. What is the new sarcomere length?
data.answer: The A-band stays constant; only the I-bands shorten.
steps: Each sarcomere has two half I-bands, so total shortening = 2 × 0.2 µm = 0.4 µm
data.caption: Sarcomere before and after contraction

data.question: Which protein binds Ca²⁺ ions to start muscle contraction?
data.description: Ca²⁺ binds troponin, which shifts tropomyosin and exposes the myosin-binding sites on actin.
data.caption: The thin filament

data.reason: Each skeletal muscle fibre forms by the fusion of many myoblasts during development.
data.explanation: Both statements are true, and the fusion of myoblasts is exactly why a single fibre carries many nuclei.

rows.myth: Muscle fibres get shorter because actin and myosin shrink
rows.factDetail: Actin slides over myosin; only the I-band and H-zone shorten.

rows.myth: Muscles can push as well as pull
rows.factDetail: Movement in both directions needs antagonistic pairs, e.g. biceps and triceps.

rows.myth: Cardiac muscle is under voluntary control
rows.factDetail: It contracts rhythmically on its own, set by the SA node.

keyPoints: Movement is a property of all living things; locomotion is movement from place to place
Muscle contraction follows the sliding filament theory
Ca²⁺ and ATP are essential for every contraction cycle
